Customers at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo report widespread outages

Customers of Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo reported widespread outages preventing normal access to online banking. Downdetector recorded a sharp spike in reports that also affected other institutions and services, including US Bank, Capital One, and Zelle.

Chase said a technical issue was causing some transactions to take longer than usual, while customers retained access to accounts and funds. Wells Fargo stated that online banking was temporarily unavailable but that accounts could still be reached via ATMs, branches, and customer service. Both banks indicated they were working to resolve the problem.

result.text:
Per Grok:

Updated timeline of the recent high-impact tech failures
Here’s the cluster as it stands (independent technical causes reported in each case):

•  Nov 12–14: Microsoft 365 global outage (Outlook, Teams, Copilot, etc.). Latent bug from a July update + network capacity issues. Affected 70+ countries. Restored by ~Nov 15.
•  Nov 13: FAA nationwide ground stop (~4–5 hours). Router/installation problem during copper-to-fiber upgrade (L3Harris contractor) flooded the air traffic control network. Thousands of delays/cancellations. Longest such stop since 9/11.
•  Nov 13–14: Workday HR/payroll outage. Disaster-recovery test connected incorrectly to production databases. Locked out users at many companies for up to ~17 hours.
•  Nov 16: Major U.S. bank online disruptions (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, Zelle, etc.). Technical issues; Chase confirmed not cyber.
•  Nov 16: United Airlines system outage (weight-and-balance / crew applications). Resolved in about an hour. Not cyber, per United and FAA.
•  Nov 15: ULA Vulcan rocket failure (lost 40 Amazon Leo satellites). First total mission loss for ULA in ~20 years.

🇺🇸Fallas en bancos de Estados Unidos: problemas para operar en Chase, Bank of America y Zelle.

❌ Una falla técnica registrada en JPMorgan Chase generó este lunes un efecto dominó en el sistema financiero estadounidense, provocando complicaciones para miles de clientes que intentaban acceder a sus cuentas digitales o realizar transferencias a través de la red Zelle.

❕El incidente también repercutió en operaciones cruzadas con otras grandes entidades como Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo y Truist.

📱 Desde Chase salieron a llevar tranquilidad respecto a la seguridad de los fondos y el origen del desperfecto. A través de un comunicado oficial en la red social X, la entidad descartó que el episodio haya sido producto de un ciberataque y precisó que el inconveniente respondió exclusivamente a fallas técnicas internas.

🗣️ «Debido a un problema técnico, algunas transacciones están tardando más de lo habitual en completarse, pero los clientes siguen teniendo acceso a sus cuentas y fondos. Estamos trabajando para resolverlo lo antes posible», sostuvo la compañía.
